summary:
MissionCraft: Launch Lab is a beginner-friendly, browser-based space mission design game built for the Space Mission Design Game challenge. Players act as a mission director and configure an Earth-observation satellite by selecting its spacecraft bus, scientific payload, power system, communications and thermal control.

The game recalculates budget, spacecraft mass, electrical power balance and communications capacity as choices change. Players must also select a launch vehicle with sufficient training payload capacity. A mission-readiness gate identifies failed constraints before a simplified launch sequence and mission report.

The prototype includes a NASA POWER data connection that retrieves historical daily solar-radiation data for Chennai as environmental context for learning about solar energy. The project aims to make engineering trade-offs tangible for students and beginners through interactive experimentation.
details:
MissionCraft: Launch Lab converts complex space mission planning into an interactive educational experience.

Players begin with Earth Observer-01, an educational satellite mission. They choose five spacecraft system categories: spacecraft bus, scientific payload, power system, communication system and thermal control.

The application calculates the overall component cost, spacecraft mass, electrical power generation and demand, and communication capacity.

Players also choose a launch vehicle. The readiness system checks the mission budget, launch vehicle payload capacity, power balance, communication requirements and system configuration. Launch is blocked until all training constraints are satisfied.

After passing the engineering checks, players can initiate a simulated countdown and receive a mission performance report.

The project uses HTML, CSS and JavaScript for the frontend, Vercel Node.js Functions for its backend, and Supabase PostgreSQL for optional cloud persistence. Browser LocalStorage provides local saving. NASA POWER daily solar-radiation data provides environmental context for the educational solar-energy component.

All game component costs, capacities, scores and engineering thresholds are illustrative gameplay values, not real spacecraft specifications.

Our future development includes lunar exploration, planetary exploration, more detailed orbital constraints and 3D spacecraft visualization.
